## Location Context

- Distance from Orlando: 60 miles east (approx. 1 hr via SR-528 Beachline Expressway)
- Distance from Kennedy Space Center: 10 minutes south
- Near: Cocoa Beach Pier, Ron Jon Surf Shop
- Ocean: Atlantic coast — soft sandy bottom, beginner-friendly 1–4 ft waves year-round
- Best for beginners: June–August (warm water 84–86°F, gentle consistent swells)
- Best overall: September–November (clean 3–5 ft Atlantic storm swells, water 78–82°F)
- Winter (Dec–Feb): biggest surf (62–68°F water), best for experienced surfers
- Water temperature range: 62°F (winter) to 85°F (summer) — no wetsuit needed 8–9 months/year
- Bottom: sandy (no reef), low-risk for beginners

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need to know how to swim to take a surf lesson?
A: You should be comfortable in the water and able to swim at least 50 meters. We start in waist-deep water and work within your comfort zone.

Q: What age can you start surfing?
A: From age 6. No upper age limit — we regularly teach adults in their 50s, 60s, and beyond.

Q: How long does it take to learn to surf?
A: Most beginners stand up in their very first lesson. Getting comfortable on green unbroken waves takes a few sessions. Reading waves and surfing consistently takes months to years.

Q: What is included in every lesson?
A: Surfboard, leash, rash guard, reef-safe sunscreen, beach safety briefing, and a certified instructor. Nothing extra to rent.

Q: How far is Cocoa Beach from Orlando?
A: About 60 miles (1 hour) east on SR-528 (Beachline Expressway). Closest ocean beach to Orlando.

Q: Can I watch a rocket launch and surf on the same day?
A: Yes. The Cape Canaveral launch pads are less than 20 miles north of our surf area. A 1–2 hour lesson fits around most launch windows. We teach from 9 AM to 5 PM daily.

Q: Is Cocoa Beach good for beginner surfers?
A: Yes, it is one of the best spots on the U.S. East Coast for learning. Gentle, consistent waves break over a soft sandy bottom — forgiving and safe for first-timers.

Q: What is the best time to surf in Cocoa Beach?
A: Fall (September–November) for the best overall conditions. Summer (June–August) is best for beginners — warmest water and gentlest waves. Winter brings the biggest surf for advanced surfers.

Q: What is the water temperature in Cocoa Beach?
A: 62°F (17°C) in winter to 85°F (29°C) in summer. A rash guard is usually enough spring through fall. A shorty wetsuit is useful December through February.

Q: Can kids do a surf lesson?
A: Yes, from age 6. Boards are sized to each child, instructors are patient and safety-focused, and parents can join in the water.

Q: What should I bring to a surf lesson?
A: Swimsuit or board shorts, towel, water bottle. Everything else — surfboard, leash, rash guard, sunscreen — is included.

Q: Private lesson or group lesson for a beginner?
A: Both work. Private ($75) gives 100% instructor focus and faster progression. Group ($60) is more social and budget-friendly. Many guests do a group first and a private to level up.

Q: How do I cancel or reschedule?
A: Flexible rescheduling up to 24 hours before your session at no charge. Contact us via WhatsApp at +1 (321) 386-9993.

Q: Where exactly are surf lessons held?
A: Beach accesses along the Cape Canaveral and south Cocoa Beach coastline. Exact meeting point confirmed at booking.

Q: Is surfing safe in Cocoa Beach?
A: Cocoa Beach is one of the safest places to surf in Florida. Sandy bottom, lifeguarded areas near the pier, and rip current education is part of every lesson.

## About the Instructor

Victor Nuñez is the founder and lead instructor of Cocosol Surf Lessons. Originally from Costa Rica, Victor has been surfing and teaching on Florida's Space Coast for years. He is ISA-certified, CPR-trained, and a certified lifeguard. He teaches in both English and Spanish and has introduced hundreds of students to surfing from complete beginners to performance-level surfers.

- Profile page: https://cocosolsurf.com/instructors/victor-nunez
